tools.name: find_business
tools.description: Searches Google Maps for a business by name, or for a kind of business, and lists the places Maps shows. Use it first when the user names a business, to get an exact placeId or cid to pass as business to the other tools; if several candidates fit, ask the user which one. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. Returns query, from (the point searched from, null when Maps chose) and candidates. Each result has position (1-based, ads not counted), sponsored, name, ids (placeId, cid, kgId, featureId, each null when Maps did not expose it), primaryCategory, rating, reviewCount, address and location (the place pin {lat, lng}), each null when the list did not show it.

query.description: The search as a customer types it into Maps, such as "Nyack Plumbing Co".

near.description: Where the search is seen from: {lat, lng}, or a place name such as "West Nyack, NY" that is looked up in Maps. Defaults to Maps' own view, which is usually the user's location.

tools.name: audit_profile
tools.description: Audits one Google Business Profile against every Local SEO check: profile basics, categories, description, services and attributes, photos, reviews, posts, the linked website and trust signals, with a 0-100 score. Use it for a profile audit or to confirm a fix. include picks what is read beyond the profile; keyword adds the relevance checks and is the competitor search. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. It can take a few minutes. Returns business (the full profile record), findings, score (an object: score, 0-100, or null when no check could be judged; judged, the number of checks judged; untested, the number not_applicable), fixes (checkId, title, severity, fix; most important first), reportMarkdown (the whole audit as a readable report) and notes on what was not read, including when Maps showed the page in a language other than English, which leaves some fields missing. The audit reads posts in the browser, which sees only the newest one, so the posting checks (L26 to L29) are not_applicable with the reason; read_posts with source dataforseo reads them all. When Maps keeps its own "Most relevant" review order, a note says so and the recency checks (L22 recent reviews, L24 reply speed, L25 recent unanswered negatives unless one was found) are not_applicable. Each finding has checkId (a Local SEO check id such as L7), group, status (pass, partial, fail or not_applicable), severity (high, medium or low on a fail or partial, null otherwise), a one-sentence summary and evidence (url, value, note). not_applicable means the check could not be judged, never that it passed or failed. A profile field the page or provider did not give is {missing: true, reason}; with absent: true it means Google was read and lists nothing there (no phone on the profile), which is a real gap, while without it the value is simply unknown. Never treat either as 0.

business.description: Which business: exactly one of {mapsUrl}, {placeId}, {cid} or {name, city}. Ids from find_business or local_scan are exact; a name and city is searched in Maps and can match a different place with the same name.

mapsUrl.description: A Google Maps link to the place, such as https://maps.app.goo.gl/... .

placeId.description: A Google place id, such as "ChIJ...".

cid.description: A Google customer id (CID), decimal digits, as in maps.google.com/?cid=.

name.description: The business name as Google shows it.

city.description: The town or city it is in, such as "Leeds, UK".

keyword.description: The search the business wants to rank for, such as "emergency plumber". Used by the relevance checks and, with include competitors, as the competitor search. Defaults to none, which leaves the keyword checks not_applicable.

include.description: What to read beyond the profile: reviews, posts, website (the linked page, for the NAP and schema checks) and competitors (the Maps results for keyword, or for the primary category without one). Defaults to ["reviews", "posts", "website"]. A part left out makes its checks not_applicable.

tools.name: read_reviews
tools.description: Reads a business's Google reviews and analyses them. Use it for review strategy, reply drafting or to judge review velocity. source picks free browser reading or paid DataForSEO, which is faster for large reads: about $0.0015 per 10 reviews. With source dataforseo it spends from the user's own DataForSEO account inside the extension, within the monthly cap set there; a call over the cap, or with no cap set, is refused with an error saying so, and the same request within the cache window the user set in the extension (7 days unless changed) is served from the cache for nothing. spend says what was charged (null when nothing paid was called). The agent never sees the key. Returns business (name, source, readAt, placeId, cid, primaryCategory, address, phone, website, rating, reviewCount; each null when unknown); reviews, one page of at most 100 (id, rating, text, publishedAt ISO or null, relativeAge as shown, ownerReply or null, authorReviewCount, photoCount); analytics over every review read (count, averageRating, distribution by star, monthly trend, velocity in the last 30, 90 and 365 days or null when no review is dated, responses with reply rate and median reply days, unansweredNegatives, photoShare and themes); read (how many were read); order (newest: newest first; most_relevant: the browser could not set Maps' Newest sort, so the reviews are Maps' "Most relevant" sample, which can skip recent ones; do not judge velocity, reply speed or recent negatives from it); truncated (true when the read holds fewer than the profile has, or stopped at max when the profile count is unknown); notes (why fewer were read or why the order is not newest, such as Google's signed-out view showing about five, only the Overview's reviews when the Reviews tab did not open, or Maps shown in a language other than English, which can leave the order unset; empty when nothing to say); and nextCursor: when not null, call again with it as cursor for the next page of the same read. A null rate or average means there were no reviews to compute it from.

cursor.description: The nextCursor from an earlier read_reviews call, to get the next page of that same read without reading Maps again. Pass the same business with it. Defaults to none, which starts a new read.

tools.name: read_posts
tools.description: Reads a business's Google posts (Updates, offers and events), newest first, and analyses how often the owner posts. Use it to judge posting cadence or before planning posts. source picks free browser reading, which sees only the newest post Maps shows on the profile's Overview, or paid DataForSEO, which reads the full list: about $0.003 per read plus $0.0015 per 10 posts. With source dataforseo it spends from the user's own DataForSEO account inside the extension, within the monthly cap set there; a call over the cap, or with no cap set, is refused with an error saying so, and the same request within the cache window the user set in the extension (7 days unless changed) is served from the cache for nothing. spend says what was charged (null when nothing paid was called). The agent never sees the key. Returns business (name, source, readAt, placeId, cid, primaryCategory, address, phone, website, rating, reviewCount; each null when unknown); posts (text, publishedAt or null, relativeAge, hasMedia, link, kind: update, offer, event or unknown); analytics (count, lastPostAgeDays, last30, last90, medianIntervalDays, gaps of over 30 days, mediaShare, linkShare, kinds; a null figure means no dated post supports it); truncated (always true from the browser); and unknown. unknown is null only when the full list was read (source dataforseo), and then an empty list is a real finding: the profile has no posts. From the browser unknown is always a sentence saying why (only the newest post was seen, or Google's signed-out view hid them): how often the business posts is unknown, not zero; say so, and offer source dataforseo.

tools.name: local_scan
tools.description: Reads the Google Maps results for a search from a point and lays them out side by side, with how often each category is used. Use it to see who wins a local search and why, or to find competitors. withDetails opens each profile for the fields the result list does not show. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. Returns results (surface, query, from, readAt and the ranked list), rows (position, sponsored, name, ids, primaryCategory, secondaryCategories, rating, reviewCount, photoCount, website, phone, claimed, address, distanceKm from the point searched from, straight line to one decimal; each null when not read or not known), categoryFrequency (category, usedBy, asPrimary, share 0-1 of rows with known categories), detailsRead and truncated (stopped at max while Maps had more). Each result has position (1-based, ads not counted), sponsored, name, ids (placeId, cid, kgId, featureId, each null when Maps did not expose it), primaryCategory, rating, reviewCount, address and location (the place pin {lat, lng}), each null when the list did not show it.

query.description: The search as a customer types it into Maps, such as "emergency plumber".

near.description: Where the search is seen from: {lat, lng}, or a place name such as "West Nyack, NY" that is looked up in Maps. Defaults to Maps' own view, which is usually the user's location.

max.description: The most results to read, 1 to 120. Defaults to 20.

withDetails.description: Open each result's profile for its secondary categories, photo count, website, phone and claimed state; slow, a few seconds per result. Defaults to false, which leaves those fields null.

tools.name: rank_at
tools.description: Runs one Maps search as if the customer stood at a point (Teleport) and says where the business ranks there. Use it to check one location, such as a customer complaint ("I can't find you from the station"); use geo_grid for an area. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. Returns at, zoom, rank and results, the top 20 at that point. A rank is {kind: "ranked", rank}, {kind: "not_found", depth} (the list was read to depth organic results, as many as Maps listed up to the cap, and the business was not there, which is not rank 0), or {kind: "unknown", reason} (the point could not be read, or Maps cut its list short, so the business may sit just past it). Each result has position (1-based, ads not counted), sponsored, name, ids (placeId, cid, kgId, featureId, each null when Maps did not expose it), primaryCategory, rating, reviewCount, address and location (the place pin {lat, lng}), each null when the list did not show it.

tools.name: geo_grid
tools.description: Maps where a business ranks across an area: a size x size grid of points spacingKm apart around center, one Maps search from each. Use it for rank diagnosis by distance. The browser source is free but slow and capped at 5x5; dataforseo allows up to 13x13 at $0.002 per point (a 7x7 grid is about $0.10). Call it first with estimateOnly true to get the price for the user to approve. With source dataforseo it spends from the user's own DataForSEO account inside the extension, within the monthly cap set there; a call over the cap, or with no cap set, is refused with an error saying so, and the same request within the cache window the user set in the extension (7 days unless changed) is served from the cache for nothing. spend says what was charged (null when nothing paid was called). The agent never sees the key. A large browser grid can take 10 minutes. Returns source, depth (results read at each point), cells (point with row, col, lat, lng; and rank), summary (points, ranked, notFound, unknown, averageRank over ranked points or null, top3Share of read points or null, best), estimatedCostUsd (null for browser) and spend. With estimateOnly, cells is empty and summary null. A rank is {kind: "ranked", rank}, {kind: "not_found", depth} (the list was read to depth organic results, as many as Maps listed up to the cap, and the business was not there, which is not rank 0), or {kind: "unknown", reason} (the point could not be read, or Maps cut its list short, so the business may sit just past it).

tools.name: category_ideas
tools.description: Finds the Google Business Profile categories that the top-ranking competitors use, how often, and which of them the business lacks. Use it to choose a primary category and secondary categories. Give business, query or both: with only a business, its primary category is the search. The top 8 competitors' profiles are opened one at a time in a background tab for their secondary categories, so it takes about a minute. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. The category counts are read from Maps for free; searchVolumes adds paid DataForSEO search volumes for each category name (one keyword task, about $0.012 plus $0.00012 per category). With source dataforseo it spends from the user's own DataForSEO account inside the extension, within the monthly cap set there; a call over the cap, or with no cap set, is refused with an error saying so, and the same request within the cache window the user set in the extension (7 days unless changed) is served from the cache for nothing. spend says what was charged (null when nothing paid was called). The agent never sees the key. Returns query, competitorsRead, categories (category, usedBy, asPrimary, share 0-1), missing (null when no business was given), volumes (category, monthlySearches or null when unknown, in the business's country, or the United States when its address names no country or no business was given; volumes itself is null unless searchVolumes was asked for and a key is set) and spend.

business.description: The business to find categories for: {mapsUrl}, {placeId}, {cid} or {name, city}. Its primary category is the search when query is not given, and missing lists what it lacks. Give business, query, or both.

mapsUrl.description: A Google Maps link to the place, such as https://maps.app.goo.gl/... .

placeId.description: A Google place id, such as "ChIJ...".

cid.description: A Google customer id (CID), decimal digits, as in maps.google.com/?cid=.

name.description: The business name as Google shows it.

city.description: The town or city it is in, such as "Leeds, UK".

query.description: The search whose top results are read, such as "plumber". Defaults to the business's primary category.

near.description: Where the search is seen from: {lat, lng}, or a place name such as "West Nyack, NY" that is looked up in Maps. Defaults to Maps' own view, which is usually the user's location.

searchVolumes.description: Add monthly search volumes for each category name, a paid DataForSEO call. Defaults to false; the category counts themselves are free.

tools.name: check_website_nap
tools.description: Checks whether a business's website states the same name, address, phone and hours as its Google profile, and whether it has LocalBusiness schema, a click-to-call link and an embedded map. Use it for NAP consistency or to check a location page. With business, the extension reads the profile from Maps and checks the website it links unless url is given. Without the extension, pass url and profile (name, and phone and address if known) and the page is fetched from this computer instead, without running its JavaScript. Returns website (url; name, address, phone and hours each with status match, mismatch, not_found (the site does not state it) or profile_missing (nothing to compare), the profile value and what the site states; localSchema with types and missing fields, or null when the page has no LocalBusiness schema; telLinks; embeddedMap), findings (checks L30 to L35), profileFrom (maps or arguments) and notes. Each finding has checkId (a Local SEO check id such as L7), group, status (pass, partial, fail or not_applicable), severity (high, medium or low on a fail or partial, null otherwise), a one-sentence summary and evidence (url, value, note). not_applicable means the check could not be judged, never that it passed or failed.

tools.name: compare_businesses
tools.description: Lays 2 to 10 Google Business Profiles side by side and measures how far the first falls behind the rest. Use it when the user names their competitors; use local_scan to find who actually ranks. keyword adds each business's Maps rank. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. Returns rows in the order given (position is that order; name, ids, categories, rating, reviewCount, photoCount, website, phone, claimed, address; each null when unknown), gap (competitors, missingCategories, primarySharedBy, and reviews, rating and photos each as target, competitorMedian, difference and known, null where a side is unknown; and summary sentences) and ranks (null without keyword). A rank is {kind: "ranked", rank}, {kind: "not_found", depth} (the list was read to depth organic results, as many as Maps listed up to the cap, and the business was not there, which is not rank 0), or {kind: "unknown", reason} (the point could not be read, or Maps cut its list short, so the business may sit just past it).

businesses.description: 2 to 10 businesses, each {mapsUrl}, {placeId}, {cid} or {name, city}. The first is the one the gap is measured for.

tools.name: profile_history
tools.description: Lists what the extension saved each time it read this profile in the past, and what changed between reads: name, categories, address, phone, website, hours, description, rating, review and photo counts, claimed state and closure. Use it to spot a suspended or edited profile, or a competitor changing its name or category. History comes from the extension storage, so a profile never read before has none. An id or link this device has seen answers without reading Google; given {name, city}, a short link, or an id the extension has not seen, Maps is opened once to learn the business's ids first. Returns snapshots (readAt and a summary, oldest first) and changes (field, before, after, from, to). A profile field the page or provider did not give is {missing: true, reason}; with absent: true it means Google was read and lists nothing there (no phone on the profile), which is a real gap, while without it the value is simply unknown. Never treat either as 0.

tools.name: local_ai_visibility
tools.description: Asks AI assistants a local buyer question, "best <query> in <city>", and reads whether each answer names the business. Use it to measure local AI visibility against competitors. source assist (the default, free) asks in the user's own signed-in browser sessions, and an engine the user is not signed in to comes back missing. source cloro asks ChatGPT, Gemini and AI Mode unattended through the user's Cloro key: about $0.014 for chatgpt and $0.012 each for gemini and ai_mode; call it first with estimateOnly true to get the price for the user to approve. A cloro run over the monthly cap, or with no key or cap set, is refused with an error saying so. Perplexity is always asked in assist mode. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. Returns prompt, source, estimatedCostUsd (null for assist) and answers (empty with estimateOnly), one per engine: engine, and answer, either {missing: true, reason} or verdict (recommended when among the first three businesses named, named when later, absent), position (1-based among businesses named, null when absent), excerpt (the passage naming it, or the opening when absent), businessesNamed, competitorsNamed and citedUrls. One run is one sample; answers change between runs.

query.description: What the customer wants, such as "emergency plumber" or "vegan bakery".

city.description: The town or city, such as "West Nyack, NY".

businessName.description: The business to look for in each answer, as people say its name.

competitors.description: Up to 10 competitor names to look for as well. Defaults to none.

engines.description: The assistants to ask: chatgpt, gemini, perplexity, ai_mode (Google AI Mode). Defaults to all four.

source.description: assist (the default) opens each assistant in the user's own signed-in browser tabs for free; the user may need to press Enter. cloro asks chatgpt, gemini and ai_mode unattended through the user's Cloro key, paid within the monthly cap set in the extension; perplexity is always asked in assist mode.

estimateOnly.description: Return only estimatedCostUsd and ask nothing, so the user can approve a cloro run first. Defaults to false.
